source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Durham campus is the anchor of North Carolina's published data center capacity, at 40 MW across 420,000 square feet of technical space.

The two numbers describe a conventional hall, not an extreme one. Forty megawatts over that floor area is about 95 watts per square foot, which is standard enterprise and cloud density. Whether the halls are built for the higher rack densities that current AI accelerators require is not published, so the campus cannot be classified as a training site on these facts alone.

The state context is what makes the facility matter. It ranks first among the five North Carolina facilities that publish a megawatt figure, and those five total 50.266 MW, so this campus is roughly 80 percent of the state's published capacity. Nineteen facilities are mapped in the state, and most publish nothing, which makes the published total a floor rather than a census.

What the data does not cover is as important as what it does. There is no address, no postal code, and no certifications, so nothing can be said about qualified tenants or compliance regimes. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power usage effectiveness. Any rack estimate depends on assumed density, roughly 1,000 racks at 40 kW or 400 at 100 kW, and those are assumptions rather than operator claims.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
